article_text_raw: 2.8-million-kwacha Constituency Development Fund disbursed to one hundred and forty community groups in Samfya district in 2026 bring the accumulative beneficiary groups to over six hundred since 2022. The event officiated by Luapila Province Deputy Permanent Secretary Evans Sikabbuba and witness by traditional leaders in the district, brought the grants limbo to an end as successful applicants received the empowerment grants. Speaking during the event Mr Sikabbuba said that the increased CDF reflects government’s commitment to decentralization by bringing resources, decision making and development closer to the communities. “Government has the annual Constituency Development Fund allocation for 1.6 million kwacha to 40.3 million per constituency. With Luapula province now having twenty constituencies, translating to more resources for community projects, skills development bursaries and empowerment.” He said.He added that government remains committed to improving service delivery, economic empowerment and livelihood in line with the decentralization agenda He ended by commending Samfya Town Council for prudent utilization of CDF resources and encouraged beneficiaries to invest responsibly for them to attain the intended cause. Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, Tabitha Chanda from the Samfya club for the disabled, thanked the state for coming to the aid of the vulnerable through programmes like the CDF. She added that the good leadership of President Hakainde Hichilema has exhibited a pro poor policies which are slowly but steadily changing the lives of the marginalised.

title_raw: GOVERNMENT BACKS SAMFYA INVESTMENT POTENTIAL WITH KEY PROJECTS
excerpt_raw: Tourism Information Center Guest Article By Marius Chisenga Economist Samfya District has, over the years, witnessed significant transformation through deliberate government interventions aimed at enhancing tourism, trade, transportation, infrastructure, and overall economic development. These investments are gradually positioning Samfya as one of the most strategic tourism and commercial centres in Luapula Province, leveraging its unique location on the… Continue reading GOVERNMENT BACKS SAMFYA INVESTMENT POTENTIAL WITH KEY PROJECTS Published September 3, 2026 Categorized as Uncategorized
article_text_raw: Guest Article By Marius Chisenga Economist Chinsanka Market Shelter Interior of Chinsanka Market shelter 124-seater passenger boat Water activities on Lake Bangweulu Samfya District has, over the years, witnessed significant transformation through deliberate government interventions aimed at enhancing tourism, trade, transportation, infrastructure, and overall economic development. These investments are gradually positioning Samfya as one of the most strategic tourism and commercial centres in Luapula Province, leveraging its unique location on the shores of Lake Bangweulu and its historical importance as a fisheries and transport hub. One of the most notable interventions is the development and rehabilitation of the Samfya Harbour. The harbour has greatly improved water transport on Lake Bangweulu, facilitating the movement of people, goods, and services between Samfya and the various island communities such as Chishi Island, Chilubi Island, Lunga, Mbabala, Kasenga, Mwelela, and many others. This improved connectivity has strengthened trade networks, enhanced access to social services, reduced transportation challenges, and created opportunities for businesses that rely on lake transport. The harbour has also reinforced Samfya’s role as a regional gateway and has become a critical piece of infrastructure supporting both economic and social development. Complementing the harbour project is the government’s investment in Sun and Sandy Lodge, which represents a significant step towards unlocking Samfya’s tourism potential. The lodge provides quality accommodation for tourists, conference delegates, government officials, and business travellers visiting the district. Beyond providing hospitality services, the lodge stimulates the local economy through the creation of employment opportunities and increased demand for locally produced goods and services. Local farmers, fishermen, vegetable growers, poultry suppliers, and other small-scale entrepreneurs stand to benefit from the lodge’s operational needs. The facility therefore acts as a catalyst for local economic participation by creating a ready market for fish, vegetables, tomatoes, fruits, and other agricultural produce from surrounding communities. Further strengthening the tourism sector is the establishment of the Tourism Information Centre. The centre serves as an important platform for marketing and promoting Samfya’s rich tourism offerings, including the beautiful beaches, Lake Bangweulu, cultural heritage sites, fishing activities, birdlife, and recreational opportunities. By providing visitors with information about accommodation facilities, tourist attractions, local events, and cultural experiences, the centre enhances the visitor experience and increases the district’s attractiveness to both local and international tourists. In the long term, the Tourism Information Centre has the potential to attract investors into the tourism sector and stimulate the growth of supporting industries such as transport, hospitality, crafts, and entertainment. Collectively, these government interventions have already begun to generate positive outcomes for the district. They have improved infrastructure and public service delivery, increased tourism activity, enhanced Samfya’s visibility as a destination for both local and international visitors, created employment opportunities, stimulated trade, strengthened economic activity, and increased the potential for local revenue generation. Furthermore, these investments send a positive signal to private investors by demonstrating government’s commitment to developing the district and creating an enabling environment for business growth. Despite these achievements, there remains considerable opportunity to maximize the benefits of these investments through targeted policy actions and institutional strengthening. One key area is capacity building and revenue enhancement for the local authority. The Council should strengthen its revenue collection systems through digitization, improved property valuation, enhanced enforcement of local levies, and continuous staff capacity development. Increased locally generated revenue would enable the Council to finance more development projects independently and reduce excessive reliance on central government transfers, which may sometimes be delayed due to competing national priorities. The district would also benefit from a comprehensive Local Economic Development (LED) Strategy that focuses on sectors with the highest growth potential. Such a strategy should prioritize fisheries and aquaculture development, tourism promotion and diversification, support for small and medium enterprises, value addition to fish and agricultural products, youth entrepreneurship, and skills development. Given Samfya’s abundant natural resources, there is significant potential to create industries that process fish and agricultural produce locally, thereby creating jobs and increasing household incomes. Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) should also be aggressively pursued to complement government investments. The Council should actively engage private investors in the development of hotels, resorts, marinas, entertainment facilities, fish processing plants, shopping complexes, and other commercial infrastructure. For example, the Tourism Information Centre could generate substantial revenue if managed through an innovative partnership with the private sector, transforming it from a purely administrative facility into a vibrant commercial and tourism promotion centre. Finally, community participation and skills development must remain central to Samfya’s development agenda. Local people should be equipped with practical skills in tourism, hospitality, business management, fisheries, aquaculture, environmental conservation, and entrepreneurship so that they can meaningfully participate in and benefit from emerging economic opportunities. Establishing a skills training institution or vocational training centre in Samfya would greatly support these efforts by producing the skilled workforce needed to sustain the district’s growing tourism, fisheries, and commercial sectors. In conclusion, government interventions such as the Samfya Harbour Project, Sun and Sandy Lodge, the Tourism Information Centre, and the construction of modern markets have laid a strong foundation for the district’s transformation. These investments have improved connectivity, stimulated tourism, enhanced trade, created employment opportunities, and increased prospects for economic growth. However, realizing the full potential of these projects will require stronger council capacity, improved revenue collection, strategic beautification efforts, robust local economic development planning, active public-private partnerships, and continued investment in skills development. With sustained commitment and effective implementation, Samfya has the potential to emerge as one of Zambia’s leading lakeside tourism destinations and economic growth centres. Marius the ngumbo village economist

article_text_raw: Students at the newly established Bangweulu School of Nursing and Midwifery in Samfya district have expressed gratitude to the government for the opportunity to pursue higher education. The school, which came to realization through the 2023 Constituency development Fund for Bangweulu Constituency brought to life a dilapidated building with modern facilities installed and a new waterborne ablution block constructed is part of the government’s quest to increase access to quality education. The youths spoken to who hail from the rural parts of Samfya; Twiingi and Katanshya communities respectively, praised government’s initiative saying it’s changing lives and opening doors to better future. Gloria Soseni a resident of Katanshya said having a facility brought in Samfya has made it possible for her to pursue her dreams of becoming a nurse. “We are happy that we have our own institution in Samfya, it is near to our homes making it easy for us to access enrolment opportunities.” Soseni said. Racheal Mwansa added a thankful note to the government for the CDF initiative saying it was not easy for her to be accepted in other institutions owing to higher population. “Am thankful to the government for expanding the CDF which has brought this school to life, giving us Samfya residents a higher chance of enrollment. The government has given us a chance to achieve our dreams, especially us students coming from the rural areas” She also extended gratitude to the school management for giving priority to Samfya applicants during enrollment. Meanwhile Astridah Mubanga gave an account of how difficult it was for her to access tertiary education from other provinces like Lusaka while Moses Bwalya added that the institution has brought many opportunities for them as students and the people of Samfya who are providing support services such as accommodation and other requisites for their stay and that of the tutoring staff. Speaking in a separate interview, the Council Secretary Handson Kachenjela echoed that Bangweulu College of Nursing and Midwifery aligns with the government’s effort to reduce inequality through education and other empowerment initiatives targeted at youths. “CDF initiative in education is aimed at bridging the gap between urban and rural areas. This institution is part of governments efforts to enhance quality education for all, employment creation and stimulation of economic growth. To ensure quality education is attained, the government has provided adequate tutoring staff, a school bus and a utility vehicle.” He spoke. The institution opened its doors to learner in June 2025 and has two cohorts with the current student population standing at ninety-nine. article_text_raw: Samfya Town Council has intensified efforts to construct and rehabilitate feeder roads in the district, aiming to improve accessibility, connectivity and trade. This move is part of the government’s ambitious quest to enhance road infrastructure with the Constituency Development Fund allocating resources. The project has been made possible owing to the availability of earth moving equipment procured using the Constituency Development Fund and over three-million-kwacha annual allocations to roads component of the fund. A total of twenty-six kilometers of township roads has so far been concluded and thirty kilometers of feeder roads opened up. This came to light when the Council Secretary Handson Kachenjela conducted spot check on the progress of the grading of feeder roads in Kalasa Mukoso of Musaba Ward. The project involves rehabilitation, grading and spot dumbing of laterite in critical artery in Mwense, Chipushi, Old Airstrip, Banda and Mwamfuli settlements of Mano and Lupili Wards respectively while feeder roads in Kalasa Mukoso and Mabo Kunda have been graded. Mr. Kachenjela highlighted the state and progress made and stated that a two million Kwacha project was contracted to the Zambia National Service, supported by the Land Development Fund from the Ministry of Lands to aided the opening up of four Kilometers of major roads in the newly created site earmarked for both residential and commercial development with over four hundred plots created in Mashinge settlement of Mano Ward in addition to the CDF funded roads. “The contractor has since completed and handed over the project to the Local Authority.” He said “The Council is excited to actualize the construction of the much-needed facility which has extensively improved the sale of plots in a newly created site in Mashinge. In addition, the construction of feeder roads is boosting economic activities especially in agriculture and fisheries while improving access to social services such as education and health care.” He added The roads construction project in Samfya is yet to be rolled out to other parts of the district owing to the availability of funds from the CDF.

article_text_raw: Mabo Kunda Maternity Annex The Permanent Secretary and other senior government officials appreciating the furniture The Permanent Secretary giving a keynote address Chinsanka Maternity annex ablution block The Constituency Development Fund (CDF) in Zambia has been instrumental in financing developmental projects in Samfya District. With the latest being Chinsanka and Mabo Kunda Communities of Kapata and Isamba wards of Bangweulu Constituency benefiting from this government budget allocation mechanism which has seen the construction of two maternity annexes in a bid to improve healthcare services and provide better facilities for the community. The construction of health facilities through CDF is expected to enhance healthcare delivery and improve the overall well-being of the community in Samfya District. The facilities have since been commissioned by the Permanent Secretary for Luapula Province Mrs. Prudence Chinama. During the commissioning of the maternity annexes, the Permanent Secretary expressed satisfaction with the stance Samfya Town Council has taken in observing the ideology of President Hakainde Hichilema and his administration on maternal health. She said that the government has put in place various measures to ensure that primary health care for the general populace is gauranteed through such interventions. Women in Mabo Kunda of Isamba ward will from henceforth have descent environment that will preserve their indignity during the prenatal, antenatal, child delivery and post-natal care. she urged expectant mothers to utilize the constructed facilities in order to safeguard the lives of their newborn. “I implore all the women and men of this locality to ensure that all expecting mothers deliver from the facilities and desist from home deliveries”. She said The facility constructed using CDF at the cost of two million two hundred and fifty-six thousand kwacha is fully furnished maternity annex, ready for use. This project has come at an opportune time as it is aimed at enhancing capacity of the health sector in the district. The human resource for the improved rural health center is guaranteed as we have constantly witnessed the massive recruitment of health workers in the country during this administration in a bid to cement and strengthen service provision. Chinsanka Rural Health Center is one of the busiest health facilities given the population magnitude of the area. The facility already plays an important role in health care delivery. The one million one hundred and eighty-one thousand maternity annex constructed will enhance the ability of the rural health center.

article_text_raw: Samfya Town Council has set tourism as a priority investment sector owing to the natural attractions that the district has. In a bid to improve the tourists and Invesment traffic in the district, the Local Authority with support from the Ministry of Tourism constructed a Tourism Information Center under the Tourism Development Fund (TDF) amounting to over two million kwacha. The facility was officially launched by the Minister of Tourism Hon. Rodney Sikumba. The facility has opened up to more investment opportunities in the district as it is serving as the information hub for the Northern Circuit Tourism.

article_text_raw: Samfya Town Council has procured four thousand two hundred and forty-nine desks for schools in all the ten wards of Samfya district amounting to over six million kwacha under the 2023 Bangweulu Constituency Development Fund. This translates to seventy percent of the total desk deficit the district registered in liaison with the department of education. This has brought excitement among the school going children as well as the general populace of Samfya. The Local Authority is working in accordance with the presidential directive and the policies of the government in the provision of descent learning environment for all children regardless of social status and locality.
